title: 长风 · Long Wind

source_analysis.finding: GitHub API identifies jbang2004/long-wind as a public repo described as a real-time wuxia action game in the browser (three.js), with homepage https://jbang2004.github.io/long-wind/, primary language JavaScript, default branch main. gh CLI was unusable in this runner (no GH_TOKEN), so unauthenticated public REST/raw endpoints were used for the same GitHub evidence.
Repository page confirms the same game identity: long-wind, wuxia action game, Play-in-browser link to the submission URL, three chapter screenshots, and full Chinese/English documentation.

README defines the game: a lone swordsman across 3 chapters (steppe at golden hour vs 断刀客, bamboo night-rain vs assassin 夜枭, lantern canal town vs 寒山客), pure three.js/WebGL, no install, open the page and play.

README documents combat depth: light/heavy combos, block and perfect parry, dodge i-frames, posture break and executions, sword qi, launches/knockdowns, lock-on, and five enemy types (archer/shieldman/spearman/assassin/bandit) plus bosses, with procedural terrain/grass/town/weather/townsfolk and zero audio files (all WebAudio synthesized).

README controls table establishes keyboard+mouse support: WASD move, mouse look, left-click slash (hold for heavy), right-click block (timed parry), Space dodge, Shift sprint, Q/Tab lock, E sword qi, F draw/sheathe, Esc pause with quality/chapter switching.

README touch section establishes mobile touch support: auto-shown ink-style virtual controls, floating left thumb-stick (push past rim to sprint), right-side drag to look, buttons for strike/dodge/block/qi/lock/draw, pause; landscape recommended; ?touch=1 forces, ?touch=0 hides.
No gamepad or device-motion controls are documented; index and README mention only keyboard/mouse and touch, so both remain unknown rather than ruled out.
Game is single-player: third-person lone swordsman vs AI enemies/bosses and scattering townsfolk AI; no multiplayer lobby, second-player input, or network play is documented anywhere.
package.json pins runtime dependency three ^0.186.0 with Vite ^8.3.0 build tooling, headless gameplay tests, and static dist build; vite.config.js uses relative base for GitHub Pages.

CREDITS attributes engine to three.js (MIT), character models to Tripo AI generation, motion capture to Adobe Mixamo (converted/retargeted by agent tools), textures/rocks to Poly Haven CC0, and states all music/sfx/voices are procedurally synthesized with no audio files.

README explicitly attributes creation: every line of code written by Claude Opus 5.5, first playable in about a day (~28h wall clock, ~19h agent time), coordinating parallel sub-agents via CONTRACTS.md and docs/BIBLE.md; character models generated with Tripo AI.

Submission URL serves the playable game shell (not just a repo or promo page): canvas#c with touch-action none, #hud overlay, brush-stroke loader, meta description 'A lone swordsman on a golden-hour grassland. Real-time three.js.', and three.js module bundles under ./assets/.

screenshots.observation: Inspected 1280x720 runtime frame: golden-hour steppe with dense wind-blown grass, low sun with haze, lone tree and mountains, three swordsmen mid-combat (one lunging, one fallen). Strong cinematic backlight and depth; best gameplay shot, placed first.

Inspected 1280x720 runtime frame: lantern-lit canal-town plaza at dusk with paifang gate, strings of red/white lanterns, stone paving, four robed figures around a swordsman whose blade flash/parry spark is frozen mid-swing. Coherent architecture and crowd staging.

Inspected 1280x720 runtime frame: night rainstorm bamboo forest with moonlit mist, stone lanterns with glowing reflections on wet ground, two distant figures and a foreground combatant; heavy rain streaks and fog soften detail.

screenshot_based_score.reason: All three inspected frames are the game's own WebGL output with coherent stylized-realistic art, cinematic lighting, and real combat staging across three distinct biomes. Above DRIFTWING (72, two atmospheric stills but one biome and no visible combat/UI) and Emberwake/Kart Royale/Turbo Kart Rally (70, dense but single-loop scenes) on variety, vegetation density, weather, and light work; above moorestech (76, catalog screenshot top with dense HUD-heavy factory views) on atmosphere and composition, though below true AAA on character close-up fidelity and HUD richness. Bamboo rain softness and lack of visible HUD slightly cap the score. Stills prove nothing about motion, performance, or feel.

reconstructed_prompt: Build a real-time third-person wuxia action game in three.js/WebGL with Vite: a lone jian swordsman across 3 chapters (golden-hour grassland, rainy night bamboo forest, lantern canal town with reactive townsfolk), light/heavy combos, block/perfect-parry, dodge i-frames, posture-break executions, sword qi, launches/knockdowns, lock-on, 5 enemy types plus 3 bosses, Mixamo mocap retargeted with IK fixes, procedural terrain/vegetation/weather/architecture, fully synthesized WebAudio music and sfx, quality tiers with TAA upscaling, touch joystick controls, demo auto-play and record-mode URL params, ~38k lines single three.js dependency, headless gameplay tests.
how_to_play: Open https://jbang2004.github.io/long-wind/ in desktop Chrome/Edge (discrete GPU best); use ?level=steppe|bamboo|town to jump chapters, ?q=low|med|high for quality.
Move with WASD, look with mouse, sprint with Shift, dodge with Space (i-frames), lock with Q/Tab.
Attack with left-click (hold for heavy), block with right-click (time it at impact for a perfect parry), fire sword qi with E, draw/sheathe with F.
Break enemy posture for executions; use launches/knockdowns and lock-on against archers, shieldmen, spearmen, assassins and chapter bosses.
Pause with Esc to change quality or chapter; on phone/tablet play landscape with the auto-shown ink touch stick (left) and strike/dodge/block/qi/lock/draw buttons (right).
mechanics: Third-person wuxia swordplay across 3 chapters and 3 bosses
Light/heavy combo chains with charged heavy slash
Block with timed perfect parry/弹反
Dodge with invincibility frames plus sprint
Sword-qi projectile and launch/knockdown crowd control
Target lock-on and enemy variety (bandit, archer, shieldman, spearman, assassin)
Reactive townsfolk AI that scatters from drawn swords
Procedural grass-wind, rain/lightning with wet reflections, lantern towns, synthesized WebAudio
Quality tiers, demo auto-play, record/orbit/slow-mo modes

rating.reason: Excluding the target, closest comparators are moorestech (64 overall, catalog top with years-long multiplayer factory systems and densest HUDs), Meridian Wake (60, playable 3-frame build with documented end-to-end systems and touch+gamepad), Emberwake (53/70, complete survivors loop with boss), DRIFTWING (52/72, ambient infinite 3D terrain tech with no fail state), and Wind & Rain (51, deep RTS loop but no verified playable host). Long Wind sits above Emberwake/DRIFTWING on gameplay depth (parry/dodge/posture/execution/lock-on, 5 enemy types, 3 bosses, 3 full biomes, townsfolk AI, 30 headless tests, ~38k lines) and above Meridian Wake on combat richness and visual variety, but just below moorestech on systems breadth, multiplayer/live-ops scale, and iteration history. Evidence gaps: judged from page HTML, README/CREDITS/package docs and 3 stills only; no interactive playthrough, so playability, balance, pacing, and sustained performance are unverified and not proven by code or screenshots.

fictional_reviews.text: The steppe at sundown stopped me mid-fight — grass hissing in the wind, then a perfect parry rang out like a struck bell. Three chapters, three duels, zero downloads.
Gorgeous ink-and-gold arena with real martial snap, but the lock-on wanders in crowds and the rain chapter turns muddy. A dazzling sketch awaiting balance and a fiercer final boss.
I sheathed my sword in the lantern town just to watch the crowd breathe again. A wuxia poem you can parry in — I have never seen a browser hold a sunset like this.
